**(d) Declared barrier transmission reading.** Under (W2), $\lambda>0$ because $W=0$ outside its compact support. Choose $R>0$ with $\operatorname{supp}W\subset(-R,R)$ and put $p_\infty:=\sqrt\lambda$. The declared scattering solution is the exact $C^2$ solution of the dimensionless equation with boundary conditions
$$u_h(\xi)=p_\infty^{-1/2}\bigl(e^{ip_\infty\xi/h}+r(h)e^{-ip_\infty\xi/h}\bigr)\quad(\xi\le-R),\qquad u_h(\xi)=p_\infty^{-1/2}t(h)e^{ip_\infty\xi/h}\quad(\xi\ge R).$$
Thus there is one incoming wave from the left and none from the right. These data determine unique amplitudes by [[thm-nrqm-controlled-dynamics-two-turn-barrier-tunnelling-error]], instantiated with its mass parameter $1/2$, potential $W$ and energy $\lambda$. Define the reference current $J_h(u):=h\operatorname{Im}(\overline u\,u')$: the normalized exterior waves have currents $\pm1$. The transmission coefficient is $T(h):=|t(h)|^2$, the ratio of transmitted to incoming reference current. The physical line-model current is a positive common multiple of $J_h$ under clause (b), so its ratio is also $T(h)$. Airy/WKB matching computes this exact boundary-defined quantity; it does not define an additional approximate scattering solution. No detector, wave packet, scattering experiment or measured count is asserted, and this clause does not by itself assert an asymptotic formula for $T(h)$.

[[def-nrqm-approximations-framework-wkb-regime-model]] with its data
$V,m,\hbar,\ell,E_\star,W,\lambda,h$ and assume hypothesis (W2): $W-\lambda$
has exactly two zeros $\xi_{a}<\xi_{b}$ on $\mathbb R$, both simple, is
strictly positive on $(\xi_{a},\xi_{b})$ and strictly negative on
$\mathbb R\setminus[\xi_{a},\xi_{b}]$. Put
$$S:=\int_{\xi_{a}}^{\xi_{b}}\sqrt{W(\xi)-\lambda}\,d\xi>0,$$
and let $T(h)$ be the model's declared transmission coefficient of its
clause (d). Then there are $h_0>0$, an $\varepsilon(h)\le C_{1}h$ for $0<h<h_0$, and a constant
$0\le C_{0}<\infty$, both depending only on the model's barrier data
$(W,\lambda,\ell,E_\star)$ and the fixed matching sections, such that
$$\Bigl|T(h)\,e^{2S/h}-1\Bigr|\le \frac{C_{0}\bigl[\varepsilon(h)+e^{-2S/h}\bigr]} {1-C_{0}\bigl[\varepsilon(h)+e^{-2S/h}\bigr]}$$
whenever the denominator is positive; consequently
$$T(h)=e^{-2S/h}\Bigl(1+O\bigl(\varepsilon(h)+e^{-2S/h}\bigr)\Bigr).$$
In the physical variables of the line model, where
$V(\ell\xi)=E_\star W(\xi)$ and $E=E_\star\lambda$, one has by
[[lem-nrqm-approximations-scaled-line-model-correspondence]] clause (b)
$$\frac{S}{h}=\frac1\hbar\int_{x_{a}}^{x_{b}}\sqrt{2m\bigl(V(x)-E\bigr)}\,dx, \qquad x_{a}=\ell\xi_{a},\ x_{b}=\ell\xi_{b},$$
so the displayed leading factor is $e^{-2S/h}
=\exp\bigl(-\frac{2}{\hbar}\int_{x_{a}}^{x_{b}}\sqrt{2m(V-E)}\,dx\bigr)$,
the exponential of minus twice the classical action integral of the forbidden
region in units of $\hbar$. The statement is conditional on the fixed
compactly supported $C^{5}$ barrier with two separated simple turning points;
rectangular walls, coalescing turning points, barrier-top uniformity and
resonant multiwell interference are excluded, and $T(h)$ is the declared
scattering-current ratio of the model, not a detector response or a measured count; no
wave packet, preparation, apparatus or sampling model is asserted. In
particular, for each fixed barrier,
$$\lim_{h\downarrow0}T(h)\,e^{2S/h}=1 .$$

[F1] **Exact local connection data.** Under (W3), the one-turn theorem supplies real exact decaying and growing solutions, normalized by dividing by their nonzero forbidden-side constants. On each fixed section away from the turn, their allowed-side values are respectively $2p^{-1/2}(\sin\Theta+O(h))$ and $p^{-1/2}(\cos\Theta+O(h))$, their forbidden-side values are respectively $\rho^{-1/4}e^{-A}(1+O(h))$ and $\rho^{-1/4}e^{A}(1+O(h))$, and the corresponding derivative estimates have the same $O(h)$ control after scaling the derivative by $h$. Here $p=\sqrt{\lambda-W}$ on the allowed side, $\rho=W-\lambda$ on the forbidden side, and $A$ is the action from the turn divided by $h$. This is [[pthm-nrqm-approximations-turning-point-connection]] clauses (a)-(c), with reflection at a turn whose derivative is negative.

Adopt the declared WKB regime model of
[[def-nrqm-approximations-framework-wkb-regime-model]] with its data
$V,m,\hbar,\ell,E_\star,W,\lambda,h$, and assume hypothesis (W3) at a
turning point $\xi_{0}$ with $W'(\xi_{0})>0$: on an interval
$[\xi_{0}-r_{0},\xi_{0}+s_{0}]$ with $r_{0},s_{0}>0$ the function
$W-\lambda$ has the single zero $\xi_{0}$, is strictly negative on
$[\xi_{0}-r_{0},\xi_{0})$ (allowed side) and strictly positive on
$(\xi_{0},\xi_{0}+s_{0}]$ (forbidden side). Write, for the two sides,
$$\theta(\xi):=\frac1h\int_{\xi}^{\xi_{0}}\sqrt{\lambda-W(\xi')}\,d\xi' \quad(\xi<\xi_{0}),\qquad \Sigma(\xi):=\frac1h\int_{\xi_{0}}^{\xi}\sqrt{W(\xi')-\lambda}\,d\xi' \quad(\xi>\xi_{0}),$$
the nonnegative dimensionless phase and exponent measured from the turning
point into the allowed and forbidden sides. Let
$$\zeta(\xi):=\operatorname{sign}(\xi-\xi_{0})\Bigl[\frac32\Bigl|\int_{\xi_{0}}^{\xi}\sqrt{|W(\xi')-\lambda|}\,d\xi'\Bigr|\Bigr]^{2/3}$$
be the Liouville coordinate. Write $R$ for the continuous remainder in the
transformed equation $w''=[\zeta/h^{2}+R(\zeta)]w$ and put
$\eta_-:=\zeta(\xi_{0}-r_{0})$, $\eta_+:=\zeta(\xi_{0}+s_{0})$. Define
$$\varepsilon(h):=C_{\mathrm{ker}}h\int_{\eta_-}^{\eta_+}\frac{|R(v)|}{\sqrt{|v|+h^{2/3}}}\,dv,$$
where $C_{\mathrm{ker}}$ is the kernel constant of
[[thm-nrqm-controlled-dynamics-stable-weighted-airy-volterra-connection]];
boundedness of $R$ on the fixed transformed interval gives
$\varepsilon(h)\le C_{1}h$ for some $C_{1}>0$ depending only on the fixed data.
There are constants $0<C_{0}<\infty$ and $0<C_{\mathrm{err}}<\infty$,
depending only on $W,\lambda,\xi_{0},r_{0},s_{0}$ (not on $h$), and $h_0>0$,
such that for every $0<h<h_0$:

(c) *Derivative and envelope control.* Let
$A_h(\zeta):=A(\zeta/h^{2/3})$ and $B_h(\zeta):=B(\zeta/h^{2/3})$ be the Airy
functions in [[thm-nrqm-controlled-dynamics-airy-envelopes-and-asymptotic-coefficients]],
let $a(\xi):=(\zeta'(\xi))^{-1/2}$, and put
$$
f_h(\zeta):=(1+|\zeta|/h^{2/3})^{-1/4},\qquad \phi_h(\zeta):=\frac{2(\zeta_+)^{3/2}}{3h}.
$$
Define the decaying and growing envelopes by
$$
e_h^-(\zeta):=f_h(\zeta)e^{-\phi_h(\zeta)},\quad d_h^-(\zeta):=h^{-2/3}f_h(\zeta)^{-1}e^{-\phi_h(\zeta)},\quad e_h^+(\zeta):=f_h(\zeta)e^{\phi_h(\zeta)},\quad d_h^+(\zeta):=h^{-2/3}f_h(\zeta)^{-1}e^{\phi_h(\zeta)}.
$$
For each transformed coordinate $\eta\in\zeta([\xi_0-r_0,\xi_0+s_0])$, define
$w_{\mathrm{dec}}(\eta):=u_{\mathrm{dec}}(\zeta^{-1}(\eta))/a(\zeta^{-1}(\eta))$
and $w_{\mathrm{grow}}(\eta):=u_{\mathrm{grow}}(\zeta^{-1}(\eta))/a(\zeta^{-1}(\eta))$.
For the solutions chosen as in the proof, the following transformed derivative
error bounds hold on the full transformed interval, with an error constant
$C_{\mathrm{err}}$ depending only on the fixed data and not on $h$:
$
|w_{\mathrm{dec}}'-A_h'|\le C_{\mathrm{err}} d_h^-(e^{\varepsilon(h)}-1),\qquad |w_{\mathrm{grow}}'-B_h'|\le C_{\mathrm{err}} d_h^+(e^{\varepsilon(h)}-1).
$
Here
$\varepsilon(h):=\varepsilon_h$ is the control parameter of [F3] and satisfies
$\varepsilon(h)\le C_1h$; the
corresponding value errors are bounded by
$C_{\mathrm{err}}e_h^-(e^{\varepsilon(h)}-1)$ and
$C_{\mathrm{err}}e_h^+(e^{\varepsilon(h)}-1)$.
Here primes on $w_{\mathrm{dec}},w_{\mathrm{grow}},A_h,B_h$ denote
$\eta$-derivatives, and primes on $a,\zeta$ denote $\xi$-derivatives.
Consequently,
$$
|u_{\mathrm{dec}}'(\xi)-a'(\xi)A_h(\zeta(\xi))-a(\xi)\zeta'(\xi)A_h'(\zeta(\xi))|\le C_{\mathrm{err}}\bigl(|a'(\xi)|e_h^-(\zeta(\xi))+|a(\xi)|\zeta'(\xi)d_h^-(\zeta(\xi))\bigr)(e^{\varepsilon(h)}-1),
$$
$$
|u_{\mathrm{grow}}'(\xi)-a'(\xi)B_h(\zeta(\xi))-a(\xi)\zeta'(\xi)B_h'(\zeta(\xi))|\le C_{\mathrm{err}}\bigl(|a'(\xi)|e_h^+(\zeta(\xi))+|a(\xi)|\zeta'(\xi)d_h^+(\zeta(\xi))\bigr)(e^{\varepsilon(h)}-1).
$$
For $\rho(\xi):=W(\xi)-\lambda>0$ on the forbidden side and
$p(\xi):=\sqrt{\lambda-W(\xi)}>0$ on the allowed side, the scaled slope
forms on every compact section bounded away from $\xi_0$ are
$$
h\rho(\xi)^{-1/4}u_{\mathrm{dec}}'(\xi)=C e^{-\Sigma(\xi)}\bigl(-1+\delta_{\mathrm{f,dec}}^{(1)}(\xi)\bigr),\qquad
h\rho(\xi)^{-1/4}u_{\mathrm{grow}}'(\xi)=C'e^{\Sigma(\xi)}\bigl(1+\delta_{\mathrm{f,grow}}^{(1)}(\xi)\bigr),
$$
$$
hp(\xi)^{-1/2}u_{\mathrm{dec}}'(\xi)=2C\bigl(-\cos(\theta(\xi)+\tfrac{\pi}{4})+\delta_{\mathrm{a,dec}}^{(1)}(\xi)\bigr),\qquad
hp(\xi)^{-1/2}u_{\mathrm{grow}}'(\xi)=C'\bigl(\sin(\theta(\xi)+\tfrac{\pi}{4})+\delta_{\mathrm{a,grow}}^{(1)}(\xi)\bigr).
$$
Each new slope error is absolute and satisfies
$|\delta_{\mathrm{f,dec}}^{(1)}|,|\delta_{\mathrm{f,grow}}^{(1)}|,
|\delta_{\mathrm{a,dec}}^{(1)}|,|\delta_{\mathrm{a,grow}}^{(1)}|
\le C_0(\varepsilon(h)+h/|\zeta(\xi)|^{3/2})$; in particular no relative
error at a sine or cosine zero is asserted.

[F2] **Airy asymptotics and envelopes.** The entire Airy functions $A,B$ of [[thm-nrqm-controlled-dynamics-airy-contour-and-fresnel-normalization]] and [[thm-nrqm-controlled-dynamics-airy-envelopes-and-asymptotic-coefficients]] satisfy $A(-Z)=\pi^{-1/2}Z^{-1/4}(\sin\Theta+O(Z^{-3/2}))$, $B(-Z)=\pi^{-1/2}Z^{-1/4}(\cos\Theta+O(Z^{-3/2}))$ for $Z\to+\infty$ with $\Theta=2Z^{3/2}/3+\pi/4$, the exponential asymptotics $A(Z)=\tfrac12\pi^{-1/2} Z^{-1/4}e^{-2Z^{3/2}/3}(1+O(Z^{-3/2}))$ and $B(Z)=\pi^{-1/2}Z^{-1/4} e^{2Z^{3/2}/3}(1+O(Z^{-3/2}))$, the Wronskian $AB'-A'B=\pi^{-1}$, and envelope bounds with $p(Z)=1+|Z|$ and $S(Z)=\tfrac23(Z_{+})^{3/2}$ ([[thm-nrqm-controlled-dynamics-airy-contour-and-fresnel-normalization]] clauses (c), (d), [[thm-nrqm-controlled-dynamics-airy-envelopes-and-asymptotic-coefficients]] clauses (a)-(c)).

[F3] **Stable Volterra connection.** Put $\eta_-:=\zeta(\xi_0-r_0)$ and $\eta_+:=\zeta(\xi_0+s_0)$, and use $A_{h}(\eta)=A(\eta/h^{2/3})$, $B_{h}(\eta)=B(\eta/h^{2/3})$, $f_h(\eta)=(1+|\eta|/h^{2/3})^{-1/4}$ and $\phi_h(\eta)=2(\eta_+)^{3/2}/(3h)$. The decaying envelopes are $e_h^-=f_he^{-\phi_h}$ and $d_h^-=h^{-2/3}f_h^{-1}e^{-\phi_h}$, while the growing envelopes are $e_h^+=f_he^{\phi_h}$ and $d_h^+=h^{-2/3}f_h^{-1}e^{\phi_h}$. The stable control parameter is $\varepsilon_h:=C_{\rm ker}h\int_{\eta_-}^{\eta_+}|R(v)|/\sqrt{|v|+h^{2/3}}\,dv\le C_1h$, with constants depending only on the fixed equation and interval. The solution with terminal Airy data $(A_{h},A_{h}')$ at the right endpoint satisfies $|w-A_{h}|\le C_{A}e_h^-(e^{\varepsilon_{h}}-1)$ and $|w'-A_{h}'|\le C_{A}d_h^-(e^{\varepsilon_{h}}-1)$; the growing branch with Airy data $(B_{h},B_{h}')$ at $\eta=0$ satisfies the analogous value and derivative bounds with $e_h^+,d_h^+$. The connection between the forbidden-side exponential forms and the allowed-side oscillatory forms carries the absolute error bounded by the respective value and derivative envelopes times $C(\varepsilon_{h}+h/|\eta|^{3/2})$ ([[thm-nrqm-controlled-dynamics-stable-weighted-airy-volterra-connection]] clauses (a)-(c), including its Facts & Assumptions (F3)).

[F4] **Allowed-region transfer on the oscillatory side.** On a closed subinterval of the allowed side bounded away from $\xi_{0}$, the exact solutions are compared with their leading WKB waves by [[thm-nrqm-controlled-dynamics-wkb-explicit-error]], with the Gronwall factor of that theorem; the side's local wavenumber is $p=\sqrt{\lambda-W}$ ([[def-nrqm-approximations-framework-wkb-regime-model]] clause (c)).

[F5] **Model identification.** The physical potential and energy are $V(\ell\xi)=E_\star W(\xi)$, $E=E_\star\lambda$, and the model equation is $u''=(W-\lambda)u/h^{2}$, so the equation, turning points and functions $\theta,\Sigma$ have the displayed dimensionless data ([[def-nrqm-approximations-framework-wkb-regime-model]] clauses (b), (c)). For either allowed or forbidden action from $\xi_0$ to a fixed point on the corresponding side, apply [[lem-nrqm-approximations-scaled-line-model-correspondence]] clause (b)(i) or (b)(ii) after removing a $\delta$-neighborhood of $\xi_0$. The square-root integrand extends continuously with value zero at the simple turning point, so letting $\delta\downarrow0$ gives the same physical-to-dimensionless identity for the displayed phase and exponent.

Here $p=\sqrt{-q}$, $S_a(x)=h^{-1}\int_a^x\sqrt q$, $S_b(x)=h^{-1}\int_x^b\sqrt q$ in the barrier, and $\Theta_l$ is the outward allowed-side action divided by $h$ plus $\pi/4$. In the one-particle model of [[post-nrqm-framework-nonrelativistic-kinematics-and-massive-particle]] with potential $V=0$, the free kinetic operators
$$K_{m}:=-\frac{\hbar^{2}}{2m}\Delta,\qquad D(K_{m})=W^{2,2}(\mathbb R^{3};\mathbb C),\qquad m>0,$$
have a massless strong-action limit: there exist a self-adjoint operator $K_{0}\ge0$ on $L^{2}(\mathbb R^{3};\mathbb C)$ with $\mathcal S(\mathbb R^3;\mathbb C)\subseteq D(K_0)$ such that $K_{m}f\to K_{0}f$ in $L^{2}$ for every $f$ in the Schwartz class $\mathcal S(\mathbb R^{3};\mathbb C)$ as $m\downarrow0$, and the formal free-plane-wave frequencies of this massive family have a finite pointwise limit at every fixed nonzero wave vector. Precisely, for $k\in\mathbb R^{3}\setminus\{0\}$ with $[k]=\ell^{-1}$, define $\omega_m(k):=\hbar|k|^{2}/(2m)$ by the plane-wave solution $e^{i(k\cdot x-\omega_m(k)t)}$ of the free equation; the additional claim is that $\lim_{m\downarrow0}\omega_m(k)$ is finite, where $[\omega_m]=\tau^{-1}$ under [[def-nrqm-framework-quantities-and-units]].

**Given:** $\hbar>0$; the spin-zero one-particle sector of P5, with $V=0$; for $m>0$ the operator $K_{m}=-\frac{\hbar^{2}}{2m}\Delta$ with domain $W^{2,2}(\mathbb R^{3};\mathbb C)$ ([[post-nrqm-framework-nonrelativistic-kinematics-and-massive-particle]] clause (iv), [[def-sobolev-space-wkp-and-its-norm]]); the free momentum operators $P_{j}$ of [[def-nrqm-magnetic-and-detection-position-and-momentum-operators]]; and the explicit normalized state $\psi_{L_0}$ of [L3].

[L4] Frequencies of the free model: for $k\in\mathbb R^{3}$, $\omega\in\mathbb R$, and $[k]=\ell^{-1}$, the smooth formal plane-wave mode $\psi_{k,\omega}(x,t)=e^{i(k\cdot x-\omega t)}$ satisfies $i\hbar\partial_{t}\psi_{k,\omega}=-\frac{\hbar^{2}}{2m}\Delta\psi_{k,\omega}$ at every point exactly when $\hbar\omega=\frac{\hbar^{2}|k|^{2}}{2m}$, that is $\omega=\frac{\hbar|k|^{2}}{2m}$, because $\partial_{t}\psi_{k,\omega}=-i\omega\psi_{k,\omega}$ and $\Delta\psi_{k,\omega}=-|k|^{2}\psi_{k,\omega}$ and the exponential does not vanish ([[thm-algebra-of-derivatives]], [[post-nrqm-framework-nonrelativistic-kinematics-and-massive-particle]] clause (iv)); the frequency has dimension $\tau^{-1}$ in the conventions of [[def-nrqm-framework-quantities-and-units]]. For $k\ne0$ this plane wave is not in $L^2(\mathbb R^3)$, so it is a formal mode rather than a normalized state.

componentwise operators $Q_{j},P_{k}$, and let $\mathcal S^{(r)}$ be its
componentwise Schwartz class
([[lem-nrqm-kinematics-componentwise-position-and-momentum]]). Units are
those of [[def-nrqm-framework-quantities-and-units]]; the unit of angular
momentum is the unit of action (J$\,$s).

**(b) Orbital angular momentum.** For $i=1,2,3$ let $L_{i}$ be the
self-adjoint operator on $H_{s}$ of
[[lem-nrqm-symmetries-rotation-generators-on-schwartz-classes]], the Stone
generator of the coordinate rotation group $t\mapsto U(R_{i}(t))$, so that
$U(R_{i}(t))=e^{-itL_{i}/\hbar}$ and, on the Schwartz class,

[[def-strongly-continuous-one-parameter-unitary-group]]). The model reads
$(L_{i},\mathrm{J\,s})$ as an **assigned sharp observable**, called the
$i$-th **orbital angular momentum** of the model, with outcome law
$\mu^{L_{i}}_{\rho}$ in a preparation $\rho$
([[def-nrqm-observables-framework-observable-and-outcome-law]] clauses (a),(b),
[[def-nrqm-state-geometry-pure-mixed-states-and-purity]]). The operators
$L_{i}$ act on the spatial factor only; their reading on the angular degrees
of freedom is the one supplied by the sphere operators
[[thm-nrqm-orbital-and-spin-orbital-self-adjoint-generators]] and
[[thm-nrqm-orbital-and-spin-sphere-onb]], and the finite-blocks identity
$\sum_{i}L_{i}^{2}F=\hbar^{2}l(l+1)F$ on the harmonic span is the content of a
separate lemma of this page
([[lem-nrqm-angular-momentum-orbital-casimir-identity]]).

**(c) Spin angular momentum.** Let $S_{i}=\hbar J_{i}$ be the internal
operators of [[def-nrqm-kinematics-framework-massive-spin-s-model]] clause
(c), the matrix actions $\bigl(S_{i}f\bigr)_{l}=\hbar\sum_{m}(J_{i})_{lm}f_{m}$
of the self-adjoint matrices of
[[prop-nrqm-orbital-and-spin-finite-spin-matrices]]. The model reads
$(S_{i},\mathrm{J\,s})$ as an assigned sharp observable, the $i$-th **spin
angular momentum**; on the internal factor,
$$[S_{i},S_{j}]=i\hbar\sum_{k=1}^{3}\varepsilon_{ijk}S_{k},\qquad S^{2}:=S_{x}^{2}+S_{y}^{2}+S_{z}^{2}=\hbar^{2}s(s+1)I$$
([[prop-nrqm-orbital-and-spin-finite-spin-matrices]] clauses (a),(b),(c),
[[post-nrqm-framework-identical-particles-and-spin]] clause (ii)). The
**ladder** operators $S_{\pm}:=S_{x}\pm iS_{y}$ and the finite projections on
the basis vectors $e_{m}$ are structural objects of the internal factor, not
assigned sharp observables, and $S_{\pm}$ are not self-adjoint. For $s=\tfrac12$
one has $S_{i}=\tfrac{\hbar}{2}\sigma_{i}$ in the Pauli matrices
([[prop-nrqm-orbital-and-spin-finite-spin-matrices]] clause (e)). The internal
factor is a finite-dimensional bookkeeping factor: it is not a spatial
coordinate, not a rotating body and not a relativistic spinor, and the model
assigns no position or worldline to it.

**(d) Total angular momentum.** For each $i$ let
$$J_{i}^{\mathrm{tot}}:=L_{i}+S_{i},\qquad D(J_{i}^{\mathrm{tot}}):=D(L_{i}),$$
the self-adjoint sum of
[[lem-nrqm-angular-momentum-su2-lift-of-the-rotation-action]] clause (c)
(well defined because $S_{i}$ is bounded and strongly commutes with $L_{i}$;
[[lem-nrqm-angular-momentum-product-flow-generator]] clause (a),
[[def-symmetric-self-adjoint-and-essentially-self-adjoint]]). The model reads
$(J_{i}^{\mathrm{tot}},\mathrm{J\,s})$ as an assigned sharp observable, the
$i$-th **total angular momentum**; its flow is the coordinate subgroup
$t\mapsto U_{s}(A_{i}(t))$ of the lifted rotation action, using the physical-axes cover $\rho(W)=C^{-1}\rho_0(W)C$ defined in that lemma (rather than the literal quaternion-coordinate cover $\rho_0$),
$U_{s}(A_{i}(t))=e^{-itJ_{i}^{\mathrm{tot}}/\hbar}$
([[lem-nrqm-angular-momentum-su2-lift-of-the-rotation-action]] clauses (b),(c)).

- **Why the sum is a definition and not a theorem.** The operator identity
  $J_{i}^{\mathrm{tot}}=L_{i}+S_{i}$ requires the strong commutation of the
  two summands for self-adjointness of the sum; that commutation and the
  product-flow identity are proved in
  [[lem-nrqm-angular-momentum-su2-lift-of-the-rotation-action]], and this
  definition only names the resulting assigned observable.
- **Orbital and spin are distinct.** $L_{i}$ acts on the spatial factor and
  $S_{i}$ on the internal factor; no term of this definition identifies the
  spin with a rotation of a spatial body, and the page proves no spin-orbit
  coupling.

Adopt the state and composition postulate P1, the observable and probability
postulate P2, the ideal conditional-measurement postulate P3, the
internal-factor assignment of the identical-particle and spin postulate P6 and
the preparation and apparatus discipline P7
([[post-nrqm-framework-state-and-composition]],
[[post-nrqm-framework-observable-and-probability]],
[[post-nrqm-framework-ideal-conditional-measurement]],
[[post-nrqm-framework-identical-particles-and-spin]],
[[post-nrqm-framework-preparation-and-apparatus]]), together with the
composite, observable and measurement readings of
[[def-nrqm-composites-framework-composite-systems-and-local-readouts]],
[[def-nrqm-observables-framework-observable-and-outcome-law]] and
[[def-nrqm-measurement-framework-declared-measurements-and-instruments]], the
angular momentum readings of
[[def-nrqm-angular-momentum-framework-angular-momentum-observables]] and the
units of [[def-nrqm-framework-quantities-and-units]]. Assume the Axiom of
Countable Choice and the Axiom of Choice, the hypotheses of the cited
mathematical suppliers. The following vocabulary is used by this page.

**(a) Declared spin-half factors.** A **declared spin-half factor** is the
internal factor $V=\mathbb C^{2}$ of the spin-$s$ model
[[def-nrqm-kinematics-framework-massive-spin-s-model]] with spin label
$s=\tfrac12$, with its orthonormal basis $(e_{+},e_{-})$, the self-adjoint
matrices $J_{i}=\tfrac12\sigma_{i}$ of
[[prop-nrqm-orbital-and-spin-finite-spin-matrices]] clause (e) and the spin
observables $S_{i}:=\hbar J_{i}$, read as assigned sharp observables with unit
$\mathrm{J\,s}$ by clause (c) of
[[def-nrqm-angular-momentum-framework-angular-momentum-observables]] and P6
clause (ii). For a unit direction $n\in\mathbb R^{3}$ put
$S_{n}:=\sum_{i}n_{i}S_{i}$. By
[[pthm-nrqm-angular-momentum-spin-spectra-and-outcome-laws]] clause (c) the
observable $S_{n}$ has the two eigenvalues $\pm\tfrac{\hbar}{2}$ with
spectral projections
$$P_{n,\varepsilon}:=\tfrac12\bigl(I+\varepsilon\,n\cdot\sigma\bigr), \qquad \varepsilon\in\Sigma=\{-1,+1\},$$
and the label $\varepsilon$ attached to the projection $P_{n,\varepsilon}$ is
the **sign label** of the outcome; the outcome coordinate is
$\varepsilon\hbar/2$, read in the unit $\mathrm{J\,s}$, while the sign label
itself is dimensionless.

**(b) Declared arrangement.** A **declared spin correlation arrangement**
consists of: the declared composite $V\widehat\otimes V$ of two declared
spin-half factors, with inclusion $\kappa$, in the sense of clause (a) of
[[def-nrqm-composites-framework-composite-systems-and-local-readouts]] (a
declared pair of distinguishable subsystems whose assigned spaces are the two
internal factors); a **declared preparation** $\rho\in D(V\widehat\otimes V)$,
the set of density operators on the composite
([[def-nrqm-state-geometry-framework-state-space]],
[[def-nrqm-state-geometry-pure-mixed-states-and-purity]]); and two unit
**setting directions** $a_{0},a_{1}\in\mathbb R^{3}$ for the first station and
$b_{0},b_{1}\in\mathbb R^{3}$ for the second station. The setting labels are
$I=J=\{0,1\}$.

**(c) Declared local sign measurements.** For the first station and setting
$i\in I$, the **declared local sign measurement** is the declared ideal sharp
measurement whose outcome structure is the pair
$(P_{a_{i},+}\otimes I,\;P_{a_{i},-}\otimes I)$ with the sign labels $\pm1$:
these are the spectral projections of the local readout of the assigned
observable $(S_{a_{i}},\mathrm{J\,s})$ on the declared composite, the local
readout being constructed through the spectral measure by clause (c) of
[[def-nrqm-composites-framework-composite-systems-and-local-readouts]] and
[[lem-nrqm-composites-local-pvm-tensor-extension]]. The second station's
declared local sign measurement for setting $j$ is
$(I\otimes P_{b_{j},+},\;I\otimes P_{b_{j},-})$, defined symmetrically.

**(d) Declared joint sign measurement and tables.** For $(i,j)\in I\times J$
the **declared joint sign measurement** of the setting pair is the declared
ideal sharp measurement of the composite whose outcome structure is
$$E_{ij}:=\bigl(P_{a_{i},\varepsilon}\otimes P_{b_{j},\delta}\bigr)_{(\varepsilon,\delta)\in\Sigma\times\Sigma}, \qquad E_{ij}(\varepsilon,\delta)=P_{a_{i},\varepsilon}\otimes P_{b_{j},\delta},$$
with the pair of sign labels as its labels: by clause (c) of
[[pthm-nrqm-angular-momentum-spin-spectra-and-outcome-laws]] each factor is an
orthogonal projection, and the tensor calculus of
[[lem-nrqm-composites-bounded-tensor-maps]] gives
$E_{ij}(\varepsilon,\delta)E_{ij}(\varepsilon',\delta')=
\delta_{\varepsilon\varepsilon'}\delta_{\delta\delta'}E_{ij}(\varepsilon,\delta)$
and $\sum_{\varepsilon,\delta}E_{ij}(\varepsilon,\delta)=I$, so this is a
finite family of mutually orthogonal projections resolving the identity, as
required by clause (a) of
[[def-nrqm-measurement-framework-declared-measurements-and-instruments]]. Its
**outcome law** in the declared preparation $\rho$ is
$$\nu^{\rho}_{ij}(\varepsilon,\delta):=\operatorname{tr}\bigl(\rho\,E_{ij}(\varepsilon,\delta)\bigr), \qquad (\varepsilon,\delta)\in\Sigma\times\Sigma,$$
read from clause (b) of
[[def-nrqm-measurement-framework-declared-measurements-and-instruments]]
(compare P2 clause (ii), [[post-nrqm-framework-observable-and-probability]]).
The **correlation table of the arrangement** is the family
$\nu^{\rho}=(\nu^{\rho}_{ij})_{(i,j)\in I\times J}$, which is a binary
correlation model on $(I,J)$ in the sense of
[[def-nrqm-bell-binary-correlation-models]] clause (a); its correlations
$E_{ij}(\nu^{\rho})$, its marginals and its CHSH functional $S(\nu^{\rho})$ are
the ones of clauses (b) and (d) of that definition, and are written
$S(\rho;a_{0},a_{1};b_{0},b_{1})$ when the arrangement data are displayed.

**(f) Scope.** Clauses (a)-(e) fix model vocabulary. They assign no spatial
position, worldline, spatial separation or temporal order to the two factors;
they assert no dynamics, no interaction, no apparatus, no detection procedure
and no measured correlation; they do not assert that the composite is prepared
by any particular laboratory procedure. Whether a laboratory arrangement
realizes the declared preparation, the declared directions and the declared
sign measurements is a tested identification with uncertainty under P7
([[post-nrqm-framework-preparation-and-apparatus]]), not a consequence of this
definition; the model's assignments of states to preparations and of spectral
projections to quantities are the readings of P1, P2 and P3 fixed on the
earlier pages.

actual_supplier_context: **Dimension bookkeeping.** [[ex-nrqm-framework-dimension-bookkeeping]] verifies that the quantities and displayed laws of the framework are dimensionally consistent under the conventions of [[def-nrqm-framework-quantities-and-units]]: coordinates, wave function, position and momentum acts, the canonical commutator, the kinetic and potential terms, the Schroedinger equation, the probability current and the boost phase. The check is bookkeeping inside the conventions: it contains no measured value and tests no physical equation against data.

**Type checks.** [[ex-nrqm-framework-quantity-type-checks]] verifies the mathematical types of the adopted objects on explicit finite-dimensional data: a pure preparation as a unit ray and as a rank-one density operator, a mixture of two orthogonal pure preparations as a density operator that is not pure, the action of a local observable on a product state, and the outcome law of a finite-spectrum observable as a probability measure on its possible values rather than a single deterministic outcome. These are internal consistency checks of the postulates; they establish no laboratory fact.

**Counterexample: the specified mass-zero limit.** [[cex-nrqm-framework-zero-mass-has-no-self-adjoint-limit]] refutes the specific assertion of a self-adjoint strong action limit on every Schwartz state together with finite limiting frequency at each fixed nonzero wave number: one explicit normalized compactly supported smooth state has diverging kinetic-operator norm, and each fixed normalized operator-domain state with nonzero momentum second moment has divergent kinetic expectation. Its model root-mean-square speed depends on mass and is not held fixed during this limit. The argument does not decide other notions of convergence or exclude independently specified massless models; the radiation extension is a separately adopted model.

**What the computations establish.** Both items are conditional statements of
declared models. [[texp-nrqm-identical-particles-two-fermion-spatial-spin-symmetry]]

species with a finite orbital factor into its spin-singlet and spin-triplet
parts, exhibits the opposite orbital exchange symmetry of the two parts, and
computes the components of an antisymmetrised product of two declared
one-particle states. [[ex-nrqm-identical-particles-exchange-versus-coulomb-terms]]
specialises a two-orbital model with a declared Coulomb-form interaction and
shows, for real normalized orthogonal $W^{1,2}$ orbitals with a nonzero
product, that the declared parallel-spin (triplet)
preparation has strictly smaller pair-interaction expectation than the singlet
preparation, the difference being twice the exchange integral.

**What they rest on.** Both rest on the adopted antisymmetric sector of P6
([[post-nrqm-framework-identical-particles-and-spin]]) in the reading of
[[def-nrqm-identical-particles-framework-species-sectors-and-preparations]]:
the assignment of the species to the antisymmetric sector and the choice of
orbital factor are model declarations, and in the second item the two orbitals
and the interaction form are declared idealizations. The spin-statistics
association is not derived, no interaction is derived from the sector and no
dynamics is introduced.

apparatus response; the terms "singlet", "triplet" and "exchange" name
components and differences of the declared models. Whether a laboratory pair
of particles is described by one of the declared preparations is a tested
identification with uncertainty under the preparation and apparatus postulate
[[post-nrqm-framework-preparation-and-apparatus]], and agreement of these
conditional numbers with data would test the combined model and apparatus
assumptions rather than prove the model.

**The two computations.** [[ex-nrqm-interference-ideal-flat-two-path-screen-distribution]]
computes, in the declared two-path model with flat product-form amplitudes, the
exact coherent and which-path probabilities of the overlap and outer regions of
the declared detection coordinate: at relative phase $\pi$ the coherent law
assigns probability zero to the whole overlap region while the balanced
which-path law assigns it positive probability, and a bin meeting a bright
region has positive coherent probability. [[ex-nrqm-interference-uniform-phase-averaging]]
shows that for orthogonal path components a declared ensemble whose relative
phase is uniformly distributed over the finitely many $n$-th roots of unity has
the which-path law with the norm weights as its averaged law. Both are
conditional computations in the declared model under the pair's detection laws
([[pthm-nrqm-interference-coherent-and-mixture-detection-laws]]); neither is a
dynamics, an environmental decoherence model, a detector response or a
statement about an apparatus.

**The reported experiment.** [[exp-nrqm-interference-bach-electron-double-slit]]
reports the primary preprint of Bach, Pope, Liou and Batelaan: a 600 eV
electron beam through a nanofabricated double-slit with slit-selective
distributions and a single-electron event build-up over 2, 7, 209, 1004 and
6235 accumulated localized events. The report supplies no calibrated
efficiency or background, no numerical localization error, no uncertainty for
its apparatus parameters, no occupancy bound and no statistical comparison
with a specified competing model; the mask-height inconsistency between its
body and its figure caption is recorded as unresolved. The item therefore
supports a qualitative operational account only, and its agreement with any
model is evidence about the combined model and apparatus assumptions, not a
proof of the framework, not a demonstration that every event is independent,
and not a demonstration that only one electron is in the apparatus at a time.

**What the page does not address.** No photon experiment is reported here; a
single-photon polarization or counting experiment belongs to the photon and
radiation page, and the classical wave comparison for light is a separate
declared model. No experiment testing the which-path or marker variants of the
arrangement is reported. No claim is made that the finite sample of the
reported experiment would distinguish the coherent from the which-path
recorded law; [[texp-nrqm-interference-finite-sample-fringe-failure]] shows
that both can fail or pass a finite-sample criterion and that coincident
recorded laws are indistinguishable by any criterion.

actual_supplier_context:
**The Gaussian packet.** [[ex-nrqm-kinematics-gaussian-position-momentum-packet]]
computes, in the spin-zero massive model, the normalized Gaussian
$\psi_{\sigma}(x)=(\pi\sigma^{2})^{-3/4}e^{-|x|^{2}/(2\sigma^{2})}$, shows
that its momentum representative is again a normalized Gaussian with width
$\sigma_{p}=\hbar/\sigma$, and evaluates the position and momentum outcome
densities of the model together with their variances $\sigma^{2}/2$ and
$\hbar^{2}/(2\sigma^{2})$ and the product $\hbar/2$. This verifies the model's
sharp laws of [[pthm-nrqm-kinematics-spin-s-outcome-laws]] on a family of
Schwartz preparations; it computes no dynamics, no measurement and no general
uncertainty statement.

**The boundary warning.** [[texp-nrqm-kinematics-dirichlet-momentum-warning]]
shows, in a hypothetical confined-model extension, that the formal interval
momentum $-i\hbar D$ on the Dirichlet domain is symmetric but not self-adjoint,
that no self-adjoint extension keeps the Dirichlet domain, and that the
Dirichlet functions are not momentum eigenfunctions of any self-adjoint
extension. Its explicit twisted-periodic extensions are
$\hbar P_{\theta}=-i\hbar D$ on the domains $u^{*}(L)=e^{i\theta}u^{*}(0)$.
The companion counterexample
[[cex-nrqm-kinematics-ccr-cannot-hold-for-bounded-operators]] shows that the
canonical commutation relation cannot hold as an identity of bounded
operators at all, so the core relation of
[[lem-nrqm-kinematics-ccr-and-internal-factor-commutation]] is genuinely a
relation on a dense core of unbounded operators rather than a bounded
operator identity.

The items of this pair are conditional consequences of the framework's
postulates and of the cited mathematics. [[def-nrqm-kinematics-framework-massive-spin-s-model]]
founds the spin-$s$ model on the state space $H_{s}=L^{2}(\mathbb R^{3};\mathbb C^{2s+1})$
with the componentwise position and momentum operators $Q_{j},P_{k}$;
[[lem-nrqm-kinematics-componentwise-position-and-momentum]] proves that these
operators are self-adjoint with their maximal domains and provides the Fourier
representation and the translation identities;
[[lem-nrqm-kinematics-ccr-and-internal-factor-commutation]] proves the
canonical commutation relations on the Schwartz core, identifies the spectral
measures and proves that the internal factor commutes with the spatial
measures; [[lem-nrqm-kinematics-momentum-representation]] constructs the
momentum representation;
[[pthm-nrqm-kinematics-spin-s-outcome-laws]] derives the position and momentum
outcome laws of the spin-$s$ model, including the Born density
$\|\psi(x)\|^{2}_{\mathbb C^{2s+1}}$ and the momentum density
$\|\psi_{p}(p)\|^{2}$;
[[pthm-nrqm-kinematics-translation-covariance]] and
[[pthm-nrqm-kinematics-boost-covariance]] establish the covariance of these
laws and of the bounded-potential dynamics under the Galilean translations and
boosts of the model's frame class. All of this is conditional on P1, P2, P4,
P5 and P6 and on the cited mathematical suppliers; none of it is a statement
that any physical system is exactly described by the model.

proves that two declared cutoff-dipole models whose mode densities agree at
the transition energy have the same rate coefficient but different
formal single-vertex photon-energy laws at every positive finite time (normalized one-photon preparations require nonzero coupling), and that a declared
sharp-line model is the idealisation approached in the limit rather than a

[[lem-nrqm-light-matter-first-order-photon-energy-law]] is the page's
mathematics: the explicit factorisation of the single-vertex emission
kernel, the normalised photon-energy law, its concentration at the transition
energy for a continuous positive mode density, and the strict positivity of
the law on windows of positive density.
[[pthm-nrqm-light-matter-first-order-emission-and-absorption-coefficients]]
proves the single-vertex emission and absorption amplitudes of the model, the
exact-model control of the one-photon level-$b$ projection probability by the

absorption from a unit one-photon vector.
[[pthm-nrqm-light-matter-golden-rule-limit-and-rate-reading]] proves the
limit of the single-vertex coefficient per unit time and declares the model
rate coefficient $\Gamma_{b}=2\pi\eta_{0}^{2}J_{b}(\Delta)/\hbar$ under a

[[pthm-nrqm-light-matter-stimulated-dipole-drive-transitions]] proves the
first-order amplitudes of the prescribed classical drive, the equal
stimulated emission and absorption coefficients for the same physical gap and prescribed real field, and
the exact identification of declared two-level Pauli data with the circular
and linear two-level drive models of the driven-dynamics page.
[[pthm-nrqm-light-matter-dipole-selection-rules]] proves the necessary
angular and parity conditions on the uncompressed dipole matrix elements, and
transfers their vanishing to compressed matrices when the declared finite-level
subspace is spanned by a finite subfamily of bound states and its declared
orthonormal basis is chosen from that same subfamily. All of these are
conditional consequences of the cited postulates, mathematics and model data;
their units are those of
[[def-nrqm-framework-quantities-and-units]].

mode assignment, no Lorentz transformation law, no massless limit of the

- [[ex-nrqm-many-body-two-site-bond-thermal-ensemble]] solves the one-particle
  two-site bond model exactly: the tunnelling-split eigenbasis, the canonical
  weights and the exact mean energy, entropy and free energy;
- [[ex-nrqm-many-body-finite-mode-noninteracting-thermal-ensemble]] evaluates
  the canonical partition sums and occupation means of two fermions in three
  modes and two bosons in two modes, with the total-occupation identity and
  ground energies checked against the page's diagonalisation theorem;
- [[ex-nrqm-many-body-gas-statistics-dilute-limits]] verifies the exact Bose
  and Fermi dilute identities, evaluated in exact rational arithmetic at
  $q=1/10$, and contrasts the finite product partition of linearly
  spaced mode energies with the divergent product of constant energies;
- [[texp-nrqm-many-body-two-site-no-thermalization]] shows, in one declared
  hypothetical preparation of the bond model, that the unitary evolution
  never produces the canonical preparation, that the site-occupation readout
  takes the canonical value $1/2$ at some times while differing from it at
  others, and that the energy readout never takes its canonical value.

None of these items contains measured data, a measured uncertainty, a
calibration, a sampling model or a detector model; all numbers are exact
model values in the declared finite-mode or countable-mode idealizations, and
the assignment of a physical system to any of these models is a tested
identification under P7
([[post-nrqm-framework-preparation-and-apparatus]]). In particular:

  assigned parameter, not a measured spectroscopic value;
- the finite-mode examples are not ideal or interacting gases; they make no

  continuum of modes;

  unitary flow; it is not evidence for or against thermalisation in nature,
  and the canonical ensemble remains the adopted assumption of
  [[post-nrqm-many-body-canonical-equilibrium-ensemble]];
- the entropy conservation used in the thought experiment is the exact
  closed-system statement of
  [[pthm-nrqm-many-body-unitary-evolution-preserves-entropy]]; it neither
  forbids nor asserts any open-system or environment-induced behaviour.

[[ex-nrqm-symmetries-free-translation-and-momentum]] is the exact free-model
computation: with $V\equiv0$ every translation is a symmetry, the free flow in
the momentum representation is the unimodular multiplier
$M_{f_{t}}$, $f_{t}(p)=e^{-it|p|^{2}/(2m\hbar)}$, the translations are the
multipliers $M_{e^{-ia\cdot p/\hbar}}$, and the momentum components are
conserved sharp observables with the law, moment and generator statements of
[[pthm-nrqm-symmetries-translation-invariance-and-momentum-conservation]];
the modulus of the momentum representative is invariant in time almost
everywhere.
[[cex-nrqm-symmetries-nonconstant-potential-breaks-translation]] shows that
this fails as soon as the potential is nonconstant in the relevant direction:
for the bounded measurable indicator potential $1_{B(0,1)}$ no nonzero
translation is a symmetry, because the shifted potential differs from the
original on a set of positive measure, so the symmetry criterion of the
translation theorem is not met.
[[ex-nrqm-symmetries-parity-selection-rule]] derives, for a potential even
almost everywhere, that every energy eigenspace is invariant under the parity
action, that a nondegenerate eigenstate has definite parity, and that the
position matrix element of two states of equal parity vanishes.
[[ex-nrqm-symmetries-central-potential-rotation-invariance]] verifies the
almost-everywhere rotational and parity invariance of a bounded radial
potential and instantiates
[[pthm-nrqm-symmetries-rotational-and-parity-invariance]]: all rotations are
symmetries, the rotation action is a strongly continuous unitary symmetry
group, and the coordinate-rotation generators $L_{i}$ are conserved sharp
observables, with the underlying conservation mechanism of
[[pthm-nrqm-symmetries-generator-conservation]].

**Apparatus resolution or error.** A finite-resolution apparatus is modeled in
this category by a declared instrument with effects and an update rule
([[def-nrqm-measurement-framework-declared-measurements-and-instruments]];
clause (iv) of P2 and the ideal conditional measurement postulate P3 in the
readings of [[post-nrqm-framework-ideal-conditional-measurement]]). Whether a
declared effect family approximates a target observable, and by how much, is a
property of the chosen instrument: the postulates do not attach a universal
error parameter to a sharp observable, and the effects alone do not determine
the update ([[pthm-nrqm-measurement-instrument-updates-not-determined-by-effects]]).

**Disturbance.** The state change produced by a measurement is likewise part
of the declared instrument: for the framework's declared ideal sharp
measurement the conditional and discarded-outcome updates are specified in
[[pthm-nrqm-measurement-projective-outcomes-and-discarded-ensembles]], and
they are idealizations, not claims about every apparatus. The framework's
postulates assign no universal disturbance to "a measurement of position" as
such.

**No conflation.** The Robertson relation bounds the product of two
preparation spreads; it does not bound an apparatus error, it does not bound a
disturbance, and it is not a statement that measuring one quantity "must"
perturb another by a fixed amount. The heuristic accounts of measurement
intrusion in the literature are accordingly used on this page at most as
motivation: the exact statements are the preparation-spread results, and the
identification of a concrete apparatus with a declared instrument is a tested
identification with uncertainty under the preparation and apparatus postulate
P7 ([[post-nrqm-framework-preparation-and-apparatus]]).

- **Why the distinction is load-bearing.** An experiment that reports a finite
  resolution, a detection efficiency or a background model is reporting
  apparatus properties; a preparation spread is a model quantity of the state
  and the assigned observable. Agreement of a measured histogram with a
  predicted distribution tests the combined preparation, apparatus and
  observable identification, not the inequality alone.
- **Disturbance is model-dependent.** Two declared instruments with the same
  outcome effects can have different updates and hence different disturbances,
  as [[pthm-nrqm-measurement-instrument-updates-not-determined-by-effects]]
  records; a disturbance claim must therefore name its instrument.

[[prop-nrqm-orbital-and-spin-finite-spin-matrices]]: for $s\in\frac12\mathbb
N$ the standard matrices $J_ze_m=me_m$ and
$J_\pm e_m=\sqrt{(s\mp m)(s\pm m+1)}\,e_{m\pm1}$ on $\mathbb C^{2s+1}$ are
self-adjoint, obey the $\mathfrak{su}(2)$ commutators, have Casimir
$J^2=s(s+1)I$, and for $s=\frac12$ are $\frac12$ times the Pauli matrices with
the multiplication law $\sigma_i\sigma_j=\delta_{ij}I+
i\sum_k\varepsilon_{ijk}\sigma_k$.
[[thm-nrqm-orbital-and-spin-symmetric-power-su2-representation]] identifies
the symmetric power of the spin-$\frac12$ module with the spin-$\frac n2$
module inside the $n$-fold tensor power;
[[thm-nrqm-orbital-and-spin-finite-spin-block-decomposition]] splits any
self-adjoint $\mathfrak{su}(2)$ triple on a finite-dimensional space into
spin blocks with the standard ladders and reads the multiplicities off
$\dim\ker(J_z-MI)$; and
[[thm-nrqm-orbital-and-spin-tensor-spin-composition]] composes two spins,
$V_s\otimes V_t=\bigoplus_{j=|s-t|}^{s+t}W_j$ with each $W_j$ unitarily
equivalent to the spin-$j$ model and an explicit ladder construction. These
finite-dimensional results feed
[[thm-nrqm-orbital-and-spin-tsirelson-bound]]: for bounded self-adjoint
involutions the Bell operator
$C=A_0\otimes(B_0+B_1)+A_1\otimes(B_0-B_1)$ satisfies
$C^2=4I-[A_0,A_1]\otimes[B_0,B_1]$ and
$|\langle C\psi,\psi'\rangle|\le2\sqrt2\|\psi\|\|\psi'\|$, the bound is
attained by the singlet with the standard settings, and the explicitly
specified common-outcome $\pm1$ model obeys the CHSH bound $2$ instead.
